At t=59 in characteristic 83, the two middle bottom derivative rows are acted on by the sixth power of the crossing matrix for each extra twist block. The eigenvalues of that sixth power are 1 and 81. Subtracting the closure identity row preserves affine dependence on 81^n, and taking a minor with one fixed row preserves it as well. findings.finding: A fresh implementation of free-word crossing updates and Fox differentiation reproduced the two displayed Laurent minors after multiplying by t^5. A fraction-free Sylvester determinant returned -83, and modular Euclidean division returned the monic gcd t+24. Evaluation at a common root supplies a nonzero Sylvester kernel vector, so this leaves exactly the candidate t=59 over characteristic 83.

Direct free-word recomputation gave h0=(10,12,60,1), h1(0)=(51,66,7,42), and h1(1)=(1,26,55,1) at the candidate. The minor pairs (48,81) and (82,75) each give 29 in the claimed combination. The inverse of 59 is 38 and the second crossing eigenvalue is 45, whose sixth power is 81. The maximal ideal reduction then proves the unit ideal statement.

The braid permutation read from the printed word is the four-cycle (0 1 3 2) in bottom-slot-to-top-slot form. The appended six crossings per step preserve this permutation. Thus the closure is a knot, and the four relators identify all meridians in abelianization, which is infinite cyclic. The Alexander module presentation uses the rank-three sum-zero edge submodule computed over the Laurent ring before passage to residue fields, so it remains valid at t=1. Its residue-field dimension bound transfers to A=Q'. The finite image ring, the Chinese remainder construction, and the simple-quotient argument give one module generator for A. Together with the meridian image it generates Q as a group.
The crossed-homomorphism product rule gives the specialized Fox equations on the four meridian values, so Lemma 2 bounds the kernel dimension by two for every field and nonzero scalar.
